browsers.note20260731: No GeoPDF completes import in Chrome 150 on this machine at any size. A 2 KB in-repo synthetic fixture reproduces the identical indefinite Reading state as a 3.2 MB real USGS file, so this is not a size threshold. Isolated to one PDF.js step: the worker streams the page operator list, emits StartRenderPage and one obj, then stops producing output; renderTask.promise never settles. Recorded as "worker stops mid-stream; render promise pending", NOT as a proven deadlock — the worker is not terminated and emits no error, and did not answer an injected liveness message, but PDF.js MessageHandler may silently drop an unrecognised action, so non-response is strong but not conclusive. Ruled out by test: file delivery (byte-exact), repo SHA, file size, registration family, HTTP server, missing PDF.js assets, asset MIME, console errors, failed requests, browser major version.

openQuestions.whyNotAProductDefect: In every case the observed behaviour is what the parser unit tests already assert, and placing a file whose CRS is in SUPPORTED_EPSG_CODES from its embedded coordinates is correct.
openQuestions.whyNoTestCatchesIt: testFixtures.test.ts asserts the manifest AGAINST ITSELF, which stays green no matter what the product does. The expected column has no behavioural oracle behind it.
openQuestions.action: Recommended, not actioned, and not approved. No fixture, manifest or test is changed. A future change should either correct the six values or bind them to real behaviour; correcting them without an oracle would only move the drift.

geoPdfApprovedRules.recommendation: AGAINST a producer-specific automatic main-map rule.
geoPdfApprovedRules.rationale: pdf-lib returns a null Producer for all 12 holdout files and ArcSOC appears in Creator instead, so producer-keyed signatures cannot match. Re-keying to Creator would define a NEW selector.
geoPdfApprovedRules.requirementForAnyFutureSelector: A freshly frozen independent holdout, LARGER than the discovery set, drawn from quadrangles not used here.
geoPdfApprovedRules.defectDefinition: A silent "first" or "largest" selection would be a defect.
